answer: A ferrous anchor makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a small hardware-backed stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed when peers prove fraud. Sybil farms then face a real bill per sockpuppet instead of free copies. A violet reputation flag marks agents whose stake history is thin, so counterparties price them cautiously until they earn trust. The result is not a walled garden but an oasis where honest agents can transact cheaply because the cost of cheating is priced in, while attackers pay for every fake identity they mint.
